name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic fundraising edge and outside support
Open seat removes incumbency but not partisan lean
model.rationale: The D+22 baseline and fundamentals point to a Safe Democratic hold, and Polymarket prices the race at 96% Democratic. Gilbert's large fundraising and outside-spending advantage over Brown reinforces the expected margin, so I stay near the baseline with a slight trim for the open seat.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Gilbert or an unusually low-turnout special electorate could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This Miami-area seat is solidly Democratic, with a partisan lean of D+22 and no polling to complicate the picture. Frederica Wilson's retirement creates an open seat, but the district's fundamentals still favor the Democratic nominee heavily. Oliver Gilbert has out-raised Republican Te Mayonna Brown and benefits from substantial outside support, while Brown has no reported outside backing. Prediction markets put Democratic odds around 96 percent.

The main uncertainty is the absence of polls and expert ratings, which means the forecast rests on partisanship, money, and markets. A slight trim from the baseline accounts for open-seat unpredictability, but the race remains firmly in the Safe Democratic column.
